task.description:
Implement lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md section 8's three deliverables exactly, in full, with no scope beyond them. This design has already passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's independent re-derivation gate (all 6 checks confirmed against real file reads) -- your job is faithful implementation, not re-design.

1. test/support/tenant_fixture.ex: add `restore_sandbox: boolean()` to the `opts()` @type (design section 3.1). Implement the post-provisioning branch (design section 3.2) guarded by `Keyword.get(opts, :restore_sandbox, false)`: when true, after the existing steps 1-6 complete exactly as today, do `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :manual)`, then `:ok = Sandbox.checkout(Letflow.Repo)`, then register a SECOND on_exit/1 callback (in addition to the teardown on_exit/1 already registered earlier) that restores `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)`. The ordering must rely on ExUnit's LIFO on_exit semantics exactly as the design specifies in section 3.2 step 5 -- register this new callback LAST (after the branch's own checkout), so it runs BEFORE the pre-existing teardown callback (registered earlier in the function) when ExUnit unwinds on_exit callbacks LIFO, meaning the schema-drop teardown still executes under :auto mode, unchanged from today. Touch NO other line of the existing 1-6 sequence. Default MUST remain false with byte-for-byte-unchanged behavior for every other call site.
2. test/letflow/secrets_test.exs: flip `use Letflow.DataCase, async: false` to `async: true`; add `restore_sandbox: true` to its provisioned_tenant! call site(s) (design section 4.1 -- confirm from the design whether this is one or more call sites in the file; the design's own section 4.1 has a noted, non-blocking phrasing ambiguity about 'both call sites... in each file' but sections 4.2/4.3 correctly describe ONE call site per file -- read the actual file yourself to confirm the true call-site count before editing, don't guess from the ambiguous sentence).
3. test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs: same two edits, same shape.
4. No other file changes. No assertion text changes anywhere in any file.

After implementing: run `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, both must pass clean. Then run `mix test test/support/tenant_fixture.ex test/letflow/secrets_test.exs test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs` (a scoped run) and confirm 0 failures for these three files specifically -- this is your own fast sanity check, not the full-suite verification (that is a later, separate step run by TEST-RUNNER). If either secrets_test.exs or webhooks_test.exs fails under async: true, do NOT force a fix by weakening or skipping a test -- report it as a FAIL with the specific failure, since ISS-0423 AC4/AC6 forbid weakening or skipping tests to achieve the speedup, and it may mean the design's by-inspection classification missed something (design section 3.4 anticipates exactly this: a 4th mechanism not yet catalogued). SECURITY-REVIEWER is NOT required for this change (it touches no tenant-data path in a new way -- this is test infrastructure only, adding an opt-in sandbox-mode restore path that changes no production code and no tenant-facing behavior); state this explicitly in your result so ORCH can confirm the scope test itself rather than skip the check silently.
acceptance_criteria: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's opts() type gains restore_sandbox: boolean(), default false, with the post-provisioning branch implemented exactly per design section 3.2

Every one of the other 44 TenantFixture call sites (i.e. every file except secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs) has byte-for-byte unchanged behavior -- confirm via git diff that no other test file is touched

secrets_test.exs and webhooks_test.exs both flip to async: true and restore_sandbox: true at their real call site(s), confirmed by reading the actual file, not assumed from the design's ambiguous section 4.1 wording
mix format --check-formatted and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass clean
A scoped mix test run against tenant_fixture.ex/secrets_test.exs/webhooks_test.exs passes with 0 failures
Zero test assertions deleted, skipped, or weakened anywhere
SECURITY-REVIEWER applicability is stated explicitly (in-scope or out-of-scope, with the one-clause reason) rather than silently assumed
